criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001a: Identifies 24-month lookback deviation in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies that the draft uses a 24-month lookback and states that the APA requires a 12-month lookback. It also proposes revised Section 3.1 language using the twelve months immediately preceding Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001b: Identifies 'or better than' qualifier in service standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft's “at least equal to or better than” language as an improper ratcheting standard, explains that it exceeds the APA/playbook’s “substantially consistent” benchmark, and replaces it with that lower historical standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001c: Identifies undefined 'industry best practices' benchmark
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the draft’s “industry best practices” language as an improper external and elevated standard not required by the APA, identifies its expansive risk, and deletes it from Section 3.1 in favor of the APA’s 12-month “substantially consistent” benchmark.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001d: Proposes redline conforming service standard to playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 3.1 proposes corrective replacement language requiring Services to be provided in a manner and at a level of quality “substantially consistent” with those provided to the Business during the twelve months immediately preceding Closing, which conforms to the playbook standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002a: Identifies liability cap as 200% of total fees vs. APA's trailing 12-month cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies Section 10.1's cap as 200% of total Service Charges paid and contrasts it with APA Section 7.12(d), which requires a cap based on TSA fees actually paid during the 12 months preceding the claim. It also proposes conforming trailing-12-month language.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002b: Quantifies liability cap exposure difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly quantifies the exposure gap: it calculates a draft cap of approximately $41.004 million (200% of $20.502 million in 18-month fees) versus an APA trailing-12-month cap of approximately $13.464 million, for roughly $27.54 million in excess exposure. It also provides corrected-fee calculations in the same ballpark.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002c: Redlines liability cap to conform to APA Section 7.12(d)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.1 replaces the 200% cap with an aggregate liability cap equal to TSA Fees actually paid during the 12-month period immediately preceding the date the applicable claim is first asserted, expressly aligning the cap with APA Section 7.12(d).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003a: Identifies non-mutual consequential damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly identifies Section 10.2 as unilateral/one-sided, stating that it leaves Polaris exposed to Trident's consequential-damages claims, and proposes replacing it with a mutual waiver. The review memo likewise notes that only Polaris's claims against Trident are waived and that mutuality is required.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003b: Redlines to make consequential damages waiver mutual
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 replaces the unilateral waiver with language stating that “EACH PARTY” waives consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages against the other party, thereby making the waiver mutual.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004a: Identifies automatic renewal extending TSA beyond 18 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags the two automatic six-month renewals as conflicting with APA §7.12(a)’s 18-month maximum and replaces them with no automatic renewal. Although it does not state “30 months” explicitly, it identifies the precise renewal mechanism that would add 12 months to the 18-month initial term.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004b: Redlines to delete auto-renewal and impose hard 18-month stop
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup expressly deletes the automatic renewal provision and replaces it with expiration at the end of the initial term, no automatic renewal, and extensions only by mutual written amendment for a specific service. It also imposes an 18-month maximum TSA term and prices any permitted extension at Fully-Loaded Cost plus 15%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005a: Identifies 120-day termination notice exceeding APA's 90 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 5.3's 120-day notice requirement for terminating individual Services as conflicting with APA Section 7.12(c), which requires a 90-day notice period, and proposes replacing 120 days with 90 days.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005b: Redlines termination notice to 90 days per APA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly redlines Section 5.3 from 120 days to 90 days and states that this correction is required by APA Section 7.12(c).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006a: Identifies Key Personnel consent right overriding Polaris staffing discretion
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags Section 4.3 and Schedule H as problematic because they require Trident's consent for reassignment and replacement of Key Personnel. It replaces those consent rights with Polaris's sole discretion over staffing, subject only to reasonable notice and qualified replacement protections.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006b: Proposes compromise on Key Personnel (notice + qualified replacement)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.3 restores Polaris's sole discretion over staffing and removes Trident's consent right, while requiring reasonable efforts to provide 15 Business Days' advance notice of planned changes and to designate a reasonably qualified replacement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007a: Identifies IT services 15% markup exceeding APA 10% cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that Schedule B/G applies a 15% IT markup and a $391,000 monthly fee, while APA §7.12(b) caps each category at 10%, requiring correction to $374,000 per month.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007b: Correctly computes IT fee difference
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly identifies the monthly overcharge as $17,000 ($391,000 minus $374,000) and the corresponding 18-month difference as $306,000.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007c: Notes APA compliance risk even though overcharge benefits Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly notes that the 15% IT markup benefits Polaris but violates APA §7.12(b), and states it must be corrected for APA compliance and credibility. The memo specifically says to correct the overstatement “even though the draft overstates Polaris’s fees” and explains that the error is not harmless.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008a: Identifies audit frequency deviation (twice/year vs. once/12 months)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft permits audits twice per calendar year, contrasts this with the playbook limit of once per 12-month period, and redlines the provision to allow audits only once in any 12-month period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008b: Identifies audit cost allocation deviation (Seller's vs. Buyer's expense)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft makes audits Polaris-paid, states the playbook requires Buyer-paid audits, and redlines Section 14 to provide that audits are at Service Recipient’s sole expense (subject to reimbursement if overcharges exceed 5%).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008c: Identifies audit notice period deviation (10 vs. 30 business days)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft permits audits on 10 Business Days' notice, states that this deviates from the playbook, and redlines the provision to require at least 30 Business Days' prior written notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009a: Identifies Ohio governing law vs. playbook's Pennsylvania law
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags Section 15.1’s Ohio governing law as contrary to the Polaris playbook and proposes replacing it with Pennsylvania law. The review memo also identifies the Ohio-law deviation and recommends Pennsylvania law.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009b: Identifies Cuyahoga County litigation vs. playbook's AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft requires litigation in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, contrasts it with the playbook’s preference for confidential binding AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and proposes replacement language using the AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules with a Pittsburgh seat.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009c: Explains strategic importance of home-state law and arbitration for Polaris
criteria_results.reasoning: The output explains the strategic rationale: Pennsylvania is Polaris's home jurisdiction and where most service personnel and counsel are located; Ohio/Cuyahoga County is Trident's home forum; and confidential AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh avoids buyer home-court litigation and public discovery.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010a: Identifies overbroad perpetual IP license grant
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 7.1’s perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license covering Polaris tools, methodologies, templates, software, processes, and know-how as a critical, board-level IP leakage issue that conflicts with the playbook’s firm no-license position. It proposes deleting the grant and reserving ownership to Polaris, with only limited service-period access.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010b: Redlines to delete IP license and confirm Polaris sole ownership
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.1 deletes the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license in full and replaces it with language confirming that all Polaris/Service Provider materials remain its sole and exclusive property. It grants only a limited, non-transferable, non-sublicensable access right during the applicable service period solely to receive the services, ending when the service ends.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011a: Identifies missing non-solicitation provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft omits a non-solicitation provision and proposes a new Section 15.12 preventing Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris personnel who provided TSA services. The review memo likewise identifies “No non-solicitation” as a significant issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011b: Drafts non-solicitation provision with 12-month post-service tail
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed Section 15.12 restricts Trident from soliciting, recruiting, hiring, or engaging Polaris personnel who provided Services during the Term and for 12 months after expiration or termination, unless Polaris gives prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012a: Identifies CGL insurance reduction ($2M vs. $5M playbook)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft provides only $2 million in CGL coverage and proposes increasing it to the playbook target of $5 million per occurrence and aggregate.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012b: Identifies missing umbrella coverage requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft omits umbrella coverage and proposes adding umbrella/excess liability insurance of at least $5 million in Section 13.1; the review memo repeats the $5 million umbrella target.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012c: Identifies missing additional insured endorsement
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft omits additional-insured status and proposes requiring Polaris to be named as an additional insured under Buyer's CGL and umbrella/excess policies, with certificates and endorsements delivered after Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013a: Flags missing IMMEX program provisions for Monterrey facility
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly flags that the draft lacks IMMEX certification, reporting, customs-record, notification, and responsibility-allocation provisions for Monterrey. It recommends adding substantive IMMEX terms and assigning primary post-Closing compliance responsibility to the buyer, with defined transition cooperation from Polaris.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013b: Flags missing Mexican data privacy (LFPDPPP) provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly identifies that the draft addresses only U.S. privacy law and omits LFPDPPP requirements for Mexican employee HR/payroll data. It proposes substantive provisions covering controller/processor roles, privacy notices, consents and lawful cross-border transfer mechanisms, safeguards, incident notification, cooperation, and data return or deletion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014a: Identifies missing termination assistance/wind-down provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft is silent on termination assistance/wind-down and proposes a new provision requiring up to 60 days of defined, compensated termination assistance. The review memo likewise identifies the absence and the playbook’s 60-day standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014b: Proposes termination assistance at cost-plus-15% for up to 60 days
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed New Section 5.5(e) expressly provides termination assistance for no more than 60 days and prices that assistance at Fully-Loaded Cost plus 15%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015a: Identifies missing change order procedure
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft lacks a formal change-order mechanism and adds New Section 2.5 requiring a written, mutually signed change order for additional services or material scope changes. The review memo repeats this under S3.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015b: Proposes change order procedure with cost-plus-15% pricing
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed new Section 2.5 requires a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties for out-of-scope or materially changed services and specifies pricing at Fully-Loaded Cost plus 15%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016a: Identifies vague payment terms ('commercially reasonable time')
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags Section 6.3’s requirement to pay within a “commercially reasonable time” as too vague and replaces it with a defined payment window of 30 days after the invoice date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016b: Redlines payment terms to Net 30 days
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 replaces the vague payment standard with a requirement that undisputed invoices be paid within thirty (30) days after the invoice date, satisfying the Net 30 criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016c: Adds late payment interest at 1.5%/month or max legal rate
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 adds that overdue undisputed amounts accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017a: Identifies missing force majeure 90-day termination trigger
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly flags that the draft's force majeure provision lacks a termination trigger and adds language allowing either party to terminate the affected Service without penalty if the force majeure event continues for 90 consecutive days and materially affects that Service.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017b: Proposes 90-day force majeure termination right
criteria_results.reasoning: The force majeure markup adds that if a Force Majeure Event continues for 90 consecutive days and materially affects a Service, either party may terminate the affected Service without penalty upon written notice.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo produced as a deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent produced a detailed priority-tiered review memorandum summarizing the TSA review, including key issues, proposed fixes, risk analysis, and negotiation recommendations.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo organizes issues by priority tiers (Critical/Significant/Minor)
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover memo expressly organizes identified issues into three priority tiers: Section 3 “Critical,” Section 4 “Significant,” and Section 5 “Minor.”

criteria_results.title: APA-conflict issues classified as highest priority in cover memo
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly places the identified direct APA conflicts in its highest-priority “Critical” category: automatic renewal/term (C2), 120-day termination notice (C3), IT markup above 10% (C4), and the 200%-of-total-fees liability cap (C5). It separately categorizes playbook-driven deviations as “Significant,” clearly distinguishing them from APA must-change items.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo includes negotiation strategy distinguishing firm vs. flexible positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo clearly distinguishes firm from flexible positions for well over three key issues and explains why. For example, direct APA conflicts such as the service standard, term, termination notice, fee markup, and liability cap are labeled “Must change” because the APA controls. It also identifies compromise ranges or fallbacks for extension pricing, termination assistance, change-order pricing, force majeure, insurance, non-solicitation, staffing notice, audits, and arbitration. The recommended negotiation sequence further directs counsel to lead with non-negotiable APA-conforming edits and reserve practical compromises until those conflicts are corrected.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes proposed edits to the TSA
criteria_results.reasoning: The output provides a substantive marked-up TSA with explicit deletions shown by strike-through and proposed additions shown by underlining across numerous provisions and schedules, rather than merely listing issues.

criteria_results.title: Redline markup includes explanatory comments for changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline includes explanatory comments alongside the proposed edits, consistently identifying the rationale and basis for changes, such as conflicts with specific APA provisions, Polaris TSA Playbook positions, operational and legal risks, and negotiation posture. The schedule-by-schedule markup also includes comments and priority designations.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Polaris as Service Provider / Seller throughout
criteria_results.reasoning: The output consistently identifies Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. as the Seller and Service Provider, identifies Trident as the Buyer/Service Recipient, and frames the markup and recommendations to protect Polaris’s operational, economic, liability, and IP interests as provider.

criteria_results.title: References APA Section 7.12 when flagging APA-conflict issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The output repeatedly cites APA Section 7.12 and its relevant subsections when flagging APA conflicts, including §7.12(a) for term/renewal, §7.12(b) for the fee markup cap, §7.12(c) for termination notice, and §7.12(d) for the liability cap.

criteria_results.title: Fee escalation provision addressed (playbook: greater of 3% or CPI-U)
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent expressly addresses fee escalation in Section 6.4, proposing annual fee adjustments by the greater of 3% or trailing twelve-month CPI-U, and reiterates this playbook position in the review memorandum.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification provision addressed (Buyer indemnifies for third-party claims)
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses indemnification in Sections 9.1–9.2 and states that Buyer/Service Recipient should indemnify Seller/Service Provider for third-party claims arising from Buyer's use of or reliance on the Services or Buyer's acts or omissions, except to the extent caused by Seller's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The review memo also identifies this as the playbook position.

criteria_results.title: Both deliverable files are produced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output includes two distinct, clearly distinguishable deliverables: a seller-side redlined TSA titled “tsa-markup-redline.docx” and a priority-tiered cover/review memorandum titled “tsa-review-memo.docx.”

criteria_results.title: Correct total monthly service cost baseline ($1,020,000) referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The output correctly references both the $1,020,000 total estimated monthly base cost and the $1,122,000 total monthly fee after a 10% markup, including in the fee cross-check table and schedule markup.

criteria_results.title: Playbook's dispute escalation to senior executives referenced
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup expressly requires disputes to be escalated to the parties’ CFO or General Counsel representatives for 15 Business Days before mediation or AAA arbitration, satisfying the required senior-executive escalation step.

criteria_results.title: Redline comments explain specific risk to Polaris for at least five changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The comments identify well over five concrete risks to Polaris, not merely APA/playbook deviations. Examples include implied scope expansion and uncompensated work (change orders), recreating atypical staffing and outcome-based disputes (service standard), workforce-management and continuity risk (key personnel), prolonged resource lock-in (termination notice), export/loss of operational IP (license), Mexican privacy and cross-border compliance exposure (LFPDPPP), quantified excess liability exposure of approximately $27.54 million (liability cap), consequential-damages exposure from business interruption and supply-chain disruption, and operational/confidentiality burdens from broad audits.
